newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yam - Asian EMU worries could hurt investment in EU.
newsitem.headline: Yam - Asian EMU worries could hurt investment in EU.

text.p: Joseph Yam, chief executive of the Hong Kong monetary authority, said on Thursday Asian concern about uncertainties surrounding European monetary union (EMU) could hurt investments from Asia into Europe.

"We are somewhat concerned about the uncertainties surrounding EMU and their possible impact on the performance of financial markets in Europe," Yam told a conference here on Hong Kong's monetary arrangements through 1997.

Yam pointed out that Asian economies are substantial holders of the world's official foreign reserves, with five out of the seven largest foreign reserves holders in the world based in Asia, managing a total of around 600 billion U.S. dollars.

"Potential considerations in the management of public funds require the adoption of risk-averse strategies, in this case possibly a reduction of exposure, with implications for the stability of financial markets in Europe, at least before the euro has been firmly established," Yam said.
